A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support matching content across the substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original RealEstate10k evaluations of DFM, SDXL, and VLM pipelines, including quantitative comparisons, ablations, qualitative examples, and appendix standard deviations.

after.justification: v2 reports original evaluations on RealEstate10k and NYU Depth V2, with quantitative comparisons, calibration analyses, ablations, and qualitative results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The three pipeline architectures are retained. A limited inference refinement changes the supplied VLM prompts from generic questions about objects left or right of the frame to explicit hypothetical 140-pixel extensions (v1 Appendix C; v2 Table 6). Expanded normalization and resizing descriptions alone do not establish additional algorithm changes.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on ten NYU Depth V2 indoor scenes, extending coverage to imagery discussed as out of distribution for DFM. The ten RealEstate10k scene/image pairs match exactly across versions. The 2D, 2.5D, and 3D tasks and the reported object-category set were already present in v1.

E2.justification: QwenVL-Chat is removed from the 2D comparison. The 3D oracle changes from receiving only in-frustum ground truth to receiving the full 3D ground-truth distribution. Other comparator families remain. ChatGPT-4o is not clearly new: v1 Appendix C already identifies it. The precise Gemini variant remains ambiguous because v2's tables name Ultra while Appendix D names Pro.

E3.justification: v2 changes the classification threshold from 1/|X| to 1.4/|X|, uses thresholded peak-to-peak distances, specifies excluding infinite distances from distance averages, and removes 2.5D accuracy reporting. Reconstruction outlier filtering changes from 10 neighbors and a 0.5 standard-deviation ratio to 20 neighbors and a ratio of 2. NYU evaluation adds camera-pose estimation and distinct preprocessing. These materially revise the reported evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: v2 adds calibration analyses relating threshold multipliers to retained points and detector confidence to bounding-box counts (Appendix A, Figures 7–8), plus expanded qualitative generation and failure examples. The principal DFM pose/sample and SDXL prompting ablation questions already existed in v1; their redistribution into separate tables is not a new analysis.

E5.justification: Standard deviations were already reported in v1 Appendix E. v2 identifies variation across scene–object combinations and newly specifies SDXL seeds and consistent seeds for DFM sample ablations. Its claim of 100 VLM queries per object, region, and scene conflicts with the stated total of 6000 = 20 × 30 × 10, so an actual increase from v1's ten repetitions cannot be established.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 substantially replace the RealEstate10k results and add NYU results. For example, the highest reported RealEstate10k 2D accuracy changes from Claude's 0.65 to SDXL's 0.918. These are revised-protocol results, not demonstrated same-setting gains. v2 also contains conflicting SDXL 2D false-negative rates: Table 1 reports zero for both datasets, whereas Tables 13–14 report 0.0385 and 0.0544.

T1.justification: The nearest-neighbor metric is substantively redefined: v1 Equation 3 compares ground-truth peaks with any above-threshold predicted location, while v2 Equation 3 compares thresholded local maxima and explicitly assigns infinity when predicted peaks are absent. The central distribution formulation and entropy definitions remain substantially equivalent; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the introduction of unobserved object detection, three generative-model-based detection pipelines, and a metric-based benchmark. Explicitly naming 2.5D in v2's abstract does not introduce a new contribution because v1 already defines and evaluates that setting. The additional dataset supplies evidence for the retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of DFM's poor NYU generalization and heatmap spillover caused by normalization, voxelization, or bounding boxes. It proposes controlled synthetic evaluation with accessible conditional distributions. The main runtime, prompt-bias, and VLM memorization limitations remain. v1's specific discussion of privacy risks and biased decisions is removed.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information: numerical filtering thresholds, voxel dimensions, resizing steps, SDXL prompt lists and rejection procedures, NYU reconstruction instructions, hardware/OS specifications, and VLM API identifiers and access dates. Code and data release remain future promises. Some added details conflict: Section 5.2 specifies 50 intermediate DFM frames and guidance 2.0, while Appendix C specifies 30 frames and guidance 2.5.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands and revises research positioning, including an explicit distinction between HOLM's active inference and this work's passive single-observation inference. It adds discussion and citations covering RenderDiffusion, DiffuScene, ALIGN, compositional reasoning, and robotic planning/exploration, while removing several earlier references. These changes extend beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work, and experimental narrative. Task definition and detection pipelines become separate sections, metrics precede experimental setup, and the appendices are reorganized and expanded. The title changes, the standalone ethics statement disappears, and reproducibility discussion is incorporated into experimental setup.

P2.justification: The document adopts a two-column layout. The original combined pipeline illustration is replaced by separate, substantially redrawn diagrams; qualitative heatmaps are revised and redistributed. Tables gain dataset groupings and inline standard deviations, with ablations separated from principal comparisons. New calibration plots, prompt/pose tables, and generation examples substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses v1's limited validation and underspecified implementation through a second dataset, calibration analyses, clearer metric edge cases, and fuller technical details. However, conflicting DFM settings between Section 5.2 and Appendix C and conflicting SDXL false-negative rates between Table 1 and Tables 13–14 undermine reproducibility and central comparisons. The PDFs do not resolve these discrepancies, so the net effect on overall quality cannot be judged reliably.
